title: On Holding 2026 Q3 Earnings Call
contentEn:
Operator: Hello, everyone. Thank you for joining us, and Welcome to the On Holding AG Q3 2026 Results. After today's prepared remarks, we will host a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star one to raise your hand. To withdraw your question, press star one again. I will now hand the conference over to Liv Radlinger, Head of Investor Relations. Liv, please go ahead.

Liv Radlinger: Good afternoon and good morning to our investor community. Thank you for joining On's third quarter earnings conference call and webcast. With me today on the call are Caspar Coppetti, Founder and Co-CEO, and Frank Sluis, CFO. David Allemann, Founder and Co-CEO, will join us for the Q & A session. Before we begin, I will briefly remind everyone that today's call will contain forward looking statements within the meaning of the federal securities laws. These forward looking statements reflect our current expectations and beliefs only and are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our annual report on Form 20-F for the 2025 fiscal year, filed with the SEC on March 3, 2026, for a detailed discussion of such risks and uncertainties. We will further reference certain non-IFRS financial measures, such as adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin.

Liv Radlinger: These measures are not intended to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the financial information presented in accordance with IFRS accounting standards. Please refer to today's release for a reconciliation to the most comparable IFRS measures. We will begin with Caspar, followed by Frank, leading through today's prepared remarks, after which we are looking forward to opening the call for the Q & A session. With that, I am very happy to turn the call over to Caspar.

Caspar Coppetti: Thank you, and a very warm welcome to everyone from Zurich. Seven weeks ago, we were thrilled to host so many of you here with us for our second Investor Day. You walked through our lab, our maker space, and our foam competence center. You watched a LightSpray upper come together in minutes, saw the design-led vision that will take our apparel business to the next level, and got a first look behind the curtain at our plans for new sports. No slide deck and no earnings call can ever bring On's culture of innovation to life quite like being here, and we are grateful to those of you who made the trip. On that stage, we made a clear commitment for the next three years: to redefine what a sportswear brand can be by running the On Premium Playbook.

Caspar Coppetti: We aim to grow faster than our industry and grow earnings even faster than sales, with the goal of making On the high-quality earnings compounder in our industry. Today, we report the first quarter of that plan, and we are thrilled with the progress that we are making. Net sales in the quarter grew close to 18% in constant currency to a record CHF 931 million, ahead of the latest expectation we provided you in September. For the first time, we have crossed CHF 900 million in a single quarter. That is more than 4x the size of the quarter in which we went public five years ago. At the same time, our underlying gross margin and adjusted EBITDA margin reached the highest levels in our history.

Caspar Coppetti: That is the On Premium Playbook doing exactly what it was built to do: growth and margin together, and not or. We delivered these results in what remains a highly promotional environment by staying true to who we are. That means leading with innovation, design, and resonant storytelling, giving our fans a unique offering that they do not find elsewhere. In a high-discount environment, there will always be some consumer choices based on price. It has never been our strategy to go for these. In such an environment, we are just as committed to premium as our highest principle. We are incredibly proud of what we have delivered this quarter, with our new technologies and styles selling strongly at full price.

Caspar Coppetti: This strategy is what allows us to reach record profitability while investing meaningfully in the three years ahead, in the technology that will run On at the scale of our 2029 ambitions, and behind football and golf ahead of their launches next year. Much of that investment lands in the second half of this year, and it is exactly what sets us up to deliver 2027 and beyond. Now, let me show you how the On Premium Playbook came to life in Q3 through the three strategic growth engines we set out in Zurich: performance led by run, lifestyle led by sneaker, and apparel led by her. In performance, we lead with run. In this quarter, the biggest innovation cycle in our history got off to a flying start, proving once again that running remains our origin and our core.

Caspar Coppetti: In Zurich, Scott told you about a day he and I spent in a run specialty store in the U.S., watching runners pick up our shoes and put them down again. We brought what we saw home, put every function around it, and built the shoe in record time, the first masterpiece of our new sensation-based franchise architecture, introducing On's breakthrough Surreal Superfoam combined with a new CloudTec geometry. That shoe is the Cloudsurfer 3, and in October, it launched with select run specialty partners. The early signals are exceptional. In its first week, the Cloudsurfer 3 sold through at more than 4x the rate the Cloudsurfer 2 did in its launch week.

Caspar Coppetti: It is already the number one model with several of our key run specialty partners, and we are pleased to see their teams so invigorated by it, introducing it to their fans with fittings, group runs, and in-store events. This momentum is fully echoed by key run influencers and industry media, who have praised the shoe as a premium leap forward for everyday runners. This is only the first shoe with our Surreal Superfoam. By the end of 2027, almost all our performance running franchises will run on one of our new supercritical foams. On's pinnacle product, the Cloudboom Strike 2, keeps showing the world what our innovation technology can do. Demand for the LightSpray version was six times greater than what we could produce, selling out in our U.S. online store on launch day. Our athletes have carried it through the autumn season.

Caspar Coppetti: A double victory in the Frankfurt Marathon was followed by a milestone in the New York City Marathon. The first time On athletes reached the podium in both the men's and the women's race at the World Marathon Major. In the Cloudmonster franchise, the laced and LightSpray Hyper, the most advanced expressions, keep taking a larger share. Runners can feel the difference the technology makes for them, and they are choosing the very best of it. These successes and the generational updates coming to our core franchises through 2027 give us strong confidence in our ability to win meaningful share in premium running, a market that continues to grow faster than the industry around it. In lifestyle, we lead with sneaker. This quarter, the Cloudtilt was again one of the fastest-growing sneaker franchises in the whole industry, and every new expression is bringing in new fans.

Caspar Coppetti: The Cloudtilt Arc launched in September and beat our plan in all three regions in its first days. In Asia Pacific, by more than 4x . In Europe, the Cloudtilt is fast becoming a Gen Z staple, taking significant share with this important consumer. The story is much bigger than one franchise. The Cloud, which also featured in our football edits, continues to show strong momentum, a true evergreen product and icon franchise. By seamlessly connecting this classic silhouette with our high-profile entry into football, we are driving significant cross-category brand heat and introducing our performance heritage to a whole new generation of lifestyle consumers. In October, two new silhouettes joined the lineup: the Cloudnova Moon Mary Jane, created with Zendaya, and already trading well above retail on resale platforms, and the sleek, lower-profile Cloudmuse, which has beaten our forecast since launch.

Caspar Coppetti: Next year comes the Cloudswift 5, our first sneaker designed from street codes up. The Cloudtilt was just the start. In apparel, we lead with her. Apparel grew 38% at constant currency, and we are on track with our goal to triple net sales over the next three years while extending our share of wallet with existing customers. Winning with her is a long game, and this quarter showed exactly how we will win it. Product designed for her in environments built around her. On the training floor, we launched new Train Tights in FormTec, a fabric developed to sculpt and shape, and backed them with our women's training campaign, and women's share of our train collection rose meaningfully.

Caspar Coppetti: Then in October came our latest collection with Zendaya, a bold design statement in python prints, and the most visible apparel moment in our history, a reach of 2.5 billion, close to 90% positive sentiment, and top styles selling out across markets within days. Retail continues to be the engine that drives our apparel ambition. In our new generation fleet, apparel share is already at least 50% higher than in our existing stores, and apparel productivity is growing faster than footwear across the whole estate, a strong validator as we look to more than double our store apparel productivity over the three-year horizon. Per product, per moments, per store. It is early, but it is working. Beyond our three strategic growth engines, we showed you in Zurich how we are building for the decades to come with new sports.

Caspar Coppetti: We are only weeks into their journey, but the earliest signals from football have been remarkable. Our announcement post became the most seen story in On's history, and in the days that followed, e-commerce sales of our campaign products more than tripled in France and more than doubled in Germany and Spain. That is the halo before we have launched a single boot. Golf follows in the first half of next year, and we will build both sports deliberately. We are thrilled with everything we have seen so far and even more excited about what lies ahead. The On Premium Playbook everywhere. That conviction ran through every channel and every region this quarter. In the Americas, the work we did with our wholesale partners over the summer, enhanced storytelling, more tech rep education, more shop-in-shops, paid off. Sellouts strongly improved from the second quarter.

Caspar Coppetti: Our partners' inventory is healthy, and the Cloudsurfer 3 has landed successfully into exactly the market we wanted. In Asia Pacific, we are building a brand that not only lasts, but is loved. That means expanding deliberately and elevating as we go, upgrading select locations, opening in some of the most in-demand premium mall locations, and adding incredible new stores in the region's greatest cities. It means the same discipline in every channel and every market, and it means engaging our fans even more directly through more than 1,000 sweat events a year. Japan shows how powerful that combination can be. In one of the world's most premium and culturally influential markets, demand for On continues to outpace supply. When our latest drop with Kith landed in September, it sold out almost immediately.

Caspar Coppetti: The very next morning, we took it to the streets of Shibuya with a community run that reached well over 1 million people organically. Every decision we make is the On Premium Playbook in action. Market-leading growth at remarkably strong margins. That margin funds investment into the superfoams, the robots, the stores, and the athletes that create the next wave of demand, enabling us to keep growing at pace from a bigger base. The margin funds innovation, the innovation earns the margin, and the loop turns again. As we said at the Investor Day, simple in principle, demanding in practice. Powerful because it compounds. Seven weeks into the plan, it is already compounding. Frank, please take us through the numbers.

Frank Sluis: Thank you, Caspar, and good afternoon, good morning, everyone. This is the first quarter of the plan we set out at our Investor Day and embodies the On Premium Playbook that we showed you there, growth and margin together. Net sales of CHF 931.4 million, a new record. A gross margin of 66.9%, excluding tariff refunds, the highest in our history. Cash of CHF 1.34 billion, up more than CHF 300 million since the start of the year. I am very pleased to walk you through the results in more detail. Net sales grew 17.8% at constant currency and 17.2% reported, and every region, every channel, and every category contributed meaningfully. Wholesale grew 13.2% at constant currency and 12.2% reported to CHF 538.2 million, and this is where much of the work we did with our partners over the summer showed up.

Frank Sluis: Sellout stepped up from the second quarter, including a strong back-to-school campaign led by our new exciting launches. In addition, several key accounts in the Americas took holiday deliveries in the final week of September that had been planned for October, business that would otherwise have landed in the fourth quarter. Through all of it, we kept selling disciplined, exactly as we said we would, and our partners are heading into the holiday season with healthy inventory levels. They can also see what is coming. The spring 2027 order book has built well, and our partners are backing our innovation pipeline with real conviction. Direct-to-consumer grew 24.8% at constant currency and 25.0% reported to CHF 393.3 million, almost twice the rate of wholesale, and another exceptional quarter. Our DTC share reached 42.2%, up 2.6 percentage points year-over-year.

Frank Sluis: You know we always set an extremely high bar for ourselves, and this quarter, we landed slightly below it. Throughout our markets, we held full price discipline despite online traffic being a little softer in a promotional environment, and a few new stores, Munich and Miami among them, now open in the fourth quarter rather than the third. With this in mind, we are very pleased with how our strategy is driving strong, high-quality growth. The share of our online customers under 24 almost doubled year-on-year, with strong increases among both men and women. In a quarter when the market around us was promotional, the youngest, most culturally influential consumers came to On, while our full price share and resulting gross margin remained market-leading. That is the next generation of fans arriving on our terms.

Frank Sluis: In retail, we opened some spectacular new stores across the globe, from Copenhagen to San Francisco. Productivity rose again, strongly led by apparel, and the store initiatives we told you about at the Investor Day drove another increase in customer satisfaction across the fleet. Turning to our regions. The Americas grew 12.4% at constant currency and reported rates to CHF 490.1 million. In North America, growth accelerated from the second quarter. We grew shelf space with our key partners and won younger consumers through back-to-school. We held our position as the brand with the highest ASP and lowest discount rate in the industry, a direct reflection of the strength of our strategy and execution. Our key accounts grew both in their existing doors and through new ones, and there is a great deal of runway left in both.

Frank Sluis: Further south, Brazil is becoming one of the most exciting stories in the region. The two stores we opened in Sao Paulo this quarter traded at more than double our forecast. When the LOEWE Cloudtilt Cosmic launched in October, Sao Paulo was the second largest city in the world for it. EMEA grew 19.1% at constant currency and 17.9% reported, and passed a  CHF 0.25 billion in a single quarter for the first time in our history. We still sometimes read EMEA described as a mature region. Look at this quarter. Every sub-region grew, and Southern Europe and the Middle East, in particular, ran well ahead of our expectations. Our Paris, Madrid, and Milan stores now trade consistently in our global top 10, alongside our London flagship.

Frank Sluis: This is a region with a lot of potential for growth, and as we set out in September, the runway ahead is long. Asia Pacific grew 31.9% at constant currency and 31.1% reported to CHF 189.9 million. This is the deliberate control pace at which we are building Asia Pacific, expanding and elevating at the same time. This includes being even more selective about how we show up with our partners in the most premium way. That is why, over the coming quarters, we expect growth closer to the mid-to-high 20s corridor we set out for the region through 2029 than in the past two years. You can already see the brand we are building. In Japan, our key partners came back to us for significantly more product through the quarter on the back of strong sellout, with reorders well ahead of what we had planned.

Frank Sluis: Both our Tokyo stores delivered exceptional results. In Korea, every store beat our expectation by at least 30%. In Sydney, we opened our first store at Bondi Junction, the epicenter of Australia's activewear movement, in an apparel-first format, and apparel took almost 30% of the sales in its opening weeks. Turning to our categories. Shoes grew 16%, apparel 38%, and accessories 40.2%. Apparel and accessories together now make up more than 9% of sales. Caspar told you the run and the sneaker stories. I want to add training, because it is one of the best examples of how authentically this brand can expand. Three years ago, training barely existed for us. This quarter, the Cloud X became our fourth-largest footwear franchise, driven by the Cloud X 5 and the Tempo, and the momentum carried into apparel.

Frank Sluis: Training apparel grew particularly strongly in the U.S., and the share of new apparel customers who found us through training nearly doubled quarter-on-quarter. Training is one of the fastest-growing sports in the world, and we have only just started. Moving down the P&L. Gross margin, excluding the tariff refund, was 66.9%, the highest in our history. Including CHF 52.6 million of U.S. tariff refunds, as we flagged in September, reported gross margin was 72.6%. Last year's third quarter included a one-time adjustment of roughly 200 basis points related to lower anticipated freight and other costs. So on a like-for-like basis, this is an exceptional underlying expansion of 320 basis points. This is first and foremost the underlying strength of our business model, as well as a modest FX tailwind. We would be proud of that margin in any quarter, but especially in such an environment.

Frank Sluis: At the Investor Day, I told you that premium is not the objective in our model, it is the mechanism. This quarter showed what that means. Our margin is the output of the On Premium Playbook, innovation that consumers choose at full price, athletes who prove it on the world's biggest stages, and experiences in our own channels that On can deliver. Execute each of those steps, and the margin follows. Full-price discipline led by our newest technologies, the sourcing and manufacturing efficiencies that come with strong execution, and the scale and the higher DTC share. That margin gives us the strength to invest in our future. SG&A, excluding share-based compensation, rose 270 basis points as a percentage of sales, and underlying adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 130 basis points to a record 21.9% when excluding one-off tariff and freight items mentioned earlier.

Frank Sluis: Every part of that investment maps back to our three year plan. Selling expenses grew with our store estate, and that is largely a mix effect. As more of our sales come through our own stores, we earn a higher gross margin and carry higher selling costs at the same time. The net effect is clearly positive. As we showed you in Zurich, retail profitability, including those costs, sits comfortably above the group margin. G&A reflects our investment in technology and expertise, the capabilities to run On at the scale of our 2029 plan. We are building the single customer view and the omnichannel capabilities Alice described at the Investor Day, and we are embedding AI deeply into how we work. That build continues in the fourth quarter. Marketing was 12.1% of sales, a bit below the run rate for this year and reflecting phasing.

Frank Sluis: Some production costs associated with our football launch, along with a number of grassroots events and partnerships, are landing in the fourth quarter. Put together, 2026 carries the upfront investment in our new sports and our technology foundations, and the material SG&A leverage in our plan builds from 2027. Turning to the balance sheet. I already mentioned our exceptional record cash position. Inventory increased to CHF 495.7 million, up 30.2% year-over-year. Within this, volumes were up just 16%, below our sales growth and a step down from the 20%-25% growth in recent quarters. The difference is largely currency translation at period end, after the U.S. dollar strengthened in September. We are well-positioned for the holiday season and for the Cloudsurfer 3 rollout in January, and weeks of supply in our partners' inventory are healthy.

Frank Sluis: Before I turn to the outlook, one more thank you to all of you who joined us in Zurich and to the On team who made it happen. Two days is a lot to ask of anyone's time, and we are very appreciative. The Investor Day was the result of a massive team effort, and it is the same team with the same spirit of collaboration that will now deliver the plan we set out there. Looking ahead, the fourth quarter has already brought some of our biggest brand moments of the year. Our latest collaborations with LOEWE and Sky High Farms, our first capsule with Burna Boy, and our athletes on the podium from Frankfurt to New York and Beijing to Kona. The openings of Miami and L.A. stores have drawn huge crowds and stellar demand.

Frank Sluis: We are reiterating our outlook for full-year net sales growth in the low 20s at constant currency. We are planning for growth to accelerate in the fourth quarter, with our holiday campaign now live and the biggest innovation cycle in our history gathering pace. We will run the holiday season the way we have run the whole year. In an expected promotional environment, we will stay true to who we are. We are excited for the important weeks ahead. The On Premium Playbook is our standard, and we will always choose the long-term health of our brand. On gross margin, we are raising our outlook from at least 65% to around 66%, excluding tariff refunds, reflecting our full price commitment, our higher DTC share, and the efficiencies that come with scale.

Frank Sluis: We will keep investing meaningfully into technology, innovation, and marketing to support the many opportunities we see ahead of us, and we expect an adjusted EBITDA margin in the range of 19.5%-20%, again, excluding tariff refunds. Including tariff refunds, we expect a gross margin of around 67.5% and an adjusted EBITDA margin in the range of 21%-21.5%. Let me close where I closed at the Investor Day. On is a high-quality earnings compounder. This was a quarter in which much of our industry traded price for volume. We did the opposite and delivered record sales, our highest underlying margins, and strong cash generation while doing it. In Zurich, growth and margin, and not or, was something we said on stage. Today, you can see it in our results. Our biggest product cycle has begun to land.

Frank Sluis: We are investing to scale it, and we are even more excited about this plan today than on the day we presented it. Thank you. Caspar, David, and I look forward to your questions.

highlights: Net sales CHF 931.4 million, +17.2% reported / +17.8% constant currency
Underlying gross margin +320 basis points on a like-for-like basis
Q4 growth expected to accelerate, predominantly DTC-led
revenueDrivers: DTC growth came from younger customers, larger footwear-and-apparel baskets, faster repeat purchasing, ten new stores, apparel expansion and strong APAC demand. Wholesale benefited from improved sell-out, new shelf space and some retailer deliveries pulled forward into Q3.
marginDrivers: Full-price discipline, higher DTC mix, sourcing and manufacturing scale, and CHF 52.6 million of U.S. tariff refunds supported margin. Excluding current tariff refunds and the prior-year freight benefit, gross margin expanded about 320 basis points.
guidance: Full-year 2026 constant-currency net sales growth remains in the low-20% range. Gross margin is expected around 67.5% including tariff refunds and around 66% excluding them; adjusted EBITDA margin is expected at 21.0%-21.5% including refunds and 19.5%-20.0% excluding them.
risks: A promotional U.S. market, quarter-to-quarter channel timing, LightSpray capacity constraints, inventory currency translation, and execution of new sports and technology investment remain the main modeling variables.
